notes: Helper-based fix covers the structural brace checks but skips the quoted address-suffix case, leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check and an unchanged "{}" branch; the segment-level tests are very thorough (backtick, heredoc, import block, leading quoted "}").

Uses the same helper approach and adds rich tests (heredoc, backtick, imports, quoted `}` at line start), but leaves a now-redundant `wasQuoted` check, does not tighten the quoted `{}` branch, and misses the address `HasSuffix` case.

Essentially matches the reference: Token helper methods are applied at every brace check, including the quoted address-suffix case and the quoted "{}" branch, and the parse tests cover nested and heredoc braces.

Essentially mirrors the reference, covering the helper methods, the address `HasSuffix` guard and the `{}` quoted-branch cleanup, and adds focused parse tests including nested blocks and heredoc braces.

Correct and complete coverage via inline `!Quoted()` checks, including the address suffix, though it is more repetitive than a helper and keeps the old quoted-"{}" branch shape; the tests are thorough at dispenser, parser and httpcaddyfile adapter level.

Complete fix that includes the address `HasSuffix` check, but it repeats inline `!Quoted()` conditions instead of a helper, leaves the quoted `{}` branch unchanged, and adds very thorough tests including an httpcaddyfile end-to-end adapter test.

Clean helper-based fix that covers dispenser and parser block logic, but it leaves the address 'ends with {' check firing on quoted addresses; the tests include the exact issue example and a NextBlock dispenser test.

Fixes the issue cleanly with unquoted-brace helper methods applied across the dispenser and parser, matching the reference except that it misses the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` check; it adds solid dispenser and parse tests.

Overengineered heuristic that statically parses import targets to decide overrides; it fails on dynamic or for_each targets and keyed module instances, has no instance-level dedup, and adds unrelated child-ordering changes (fails one hidden test).

Fixes the root-module for_each case, but it keeps config-time deduplication through static address parsing, so parent-over-child precedence breaks when modules are keyed (child blocks can overwrite parent ones); it also adds unrelated child sorting and is more complex than needed.

Fixes the root-module for_each case, but still dedupes on ConfigResource across ancestor modules, so a parent block for one instance silently drops a child block for a different instance (fails 2 of 3 hidden tests).
Only exempts same-module blocks from deduplication, so an ancestor block still suppresses child blocks targeting different instances of the same resource; this fails most hidden tests.

Matches the reference: returns all statements unchanged and moves parent-over-child precedence to instance-level dedup in expandResourceImports, plus a defensive fix for slice aliasing; the test is a clear regression test for the issue.

Matches the reference: it returns all statements in parent-first order and deduplicates per resource instance in `expandResourceImports`, plus a small harmless fix for slice aliasing and a solid regression test.

Works by visiting children before parents so the parent's later knownImports.Put overwrites the child's, which passes all tests but depends on implicit last-write-wins ordering instead of an explicit instance-level check.

Returns every import statement and visits children first, so the parent's later `knownImports.Put` overwrites the child's; this is correct and minimal, but precedence depends on implicit ordering and map overwrite rather than an explicit instance-level check.
